To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mechanical properties of nanoscale Zr/Nb composites can be tailored by the combination of the grain size and radiation damage.
Zr/Nb nanocomposites are radiation hardenable by γ-rays and that this effect is enhanced with the reduction in periodicity.
the Zr/Nb nanolayered multilayers are promising materials for radiation hardening applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of ionizing radiation on mechanical properties of Zr/Nb nanocomposites.
a study of the structural and mechanical properties of Zr/Nb metallic multilayers before and after γ-irradiation.
the effect of γ-radiation on the mechanical properties of multilayer nanomaterials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed radiation hardenability of Zr/Nb MLs is mainly due to the presence of the Nb layers, which have a higher radiation sensitivity and are more prone to the radiation hardening effect.
the observed radiation hardenability of Zr/Nb MLNCs is mainly due to the radiation induced defects in Nb layers.

the hardness of the nanocomposites is increased after irradiation, and this is mainly due to the increase in compressive stresses in the Nb layers, which are the harder phase of the multilayer system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radiation-induced hardening is more effective in multilayers with smaller period.

the radiation hardening effect is a result of a complex interplay between the radiation-induced defects and the structural features of the multilayer nanomaterials, which can be controlled by the multilayer periodicity.

the mechanical response of multilayer nanolaminate systems can be tailored through the choice of the layer materials, the layer thickness, the grain size, the defect density distribution, the interface characteristics, etc.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the radiation-induced hardening effect can be controlled by the choice of the multilayer periodicity.
the hardness of Zr/Nb nanocomposites can be enhanced by the combined effects of the grain size and radiation induced defect density.
the mechanical properties of Zr/Nb nanocomposites could be tailored by controlling the periodicity of the multilayers and the irradiation conditions.
